why: mediopassive verbs are A2 Unit 31 (a2-155) and meg- A2 Unit 22 (a2-108): presented as new; the screen claims -ódik but shows -ul and bare verbs

old: To describe how food cooks and transforms, Hungarian employs mediopassive verbs (*-ódik / -ődik*) and inchoative verbs (*-ul / -ül*): *megsül* (bakes/roasts), *megfő* (cooks/boils), *megpuhul* (becomes soft/tender), *összekeveredik* (gets mixed together), *elkészül* (gets completed/done).
new: You know from A2 Units 22 and 31 that a prefix such as *meg-* can mark a finished action, and that some verbs say that something happens by itself. In cooking, compare *fő* (is cooking) and *megfő* (gets done), *sül* (is baking) and *megsül* (gets done); a person *főz* or *süt* it. Also *megpuhul* (becomes soft) and *elkészül* (gets ready).
why: recap; the bare forms fő/sül and főz/süt are italicised so they count as met
